Marissa — draft language below you can paste into the annex; attaching a formatted template as well. High-level points:

- Legal basis / transfer mechanism: Redwood proposes a contractual transfer approach using the most recent EU SCCs where applicable, supplemented by an APAC contractual addendum for customers in jurisdictions without adequacy findings. For APAC->US processing we rely on SCCs (or equivalent contractual safeguards) together with documented technical and organisational measures (encryption in transit, role-based access controls, restricted subprocessor list).

- Caching & persistence: Short-lived inference caches (KV/prefix caches) are resident in the serving region (e.g., Singapore) and are ephemeral by design. Persistent storage of logs and telemetry occurs only in configured regions; by default, embeddings and application outputs processed for Redwood-hosted customers are retained in the primary processing region unless otherwise requested. We will explicitly state that transient caches are not written to durable object storage except for operational diagnostic snapshots (retention <= 30 days, on request).

- KMS / key custody: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations. Draft annex text: "Customer may supply and maintain cryptographic keys via supported KMS; Redwood will never persist plaintext keys and will limit access to keys for cryptographic operations only."

- Incident notification & retention: Incident notifications follow our standard SLA: initial notification within 72 hours of detection to designated customer contacts; full incident report within 10 business days. Log retention windows: default 90 days for operational logs; customizable per customer contract.

Attachments: [DPA-Annex-Template-priya.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

If you want tighter retention or faster notification windows for HealthPort, propose specifics and we can confirm.

—Karthik
